newsitem.title: GREECE: Turkish pilot safe after bailing out - Greek radios.
newsitem.headline: Turkish pilot safe after bailing out - Greek radios.

text.p: Greek naval forces on Tuesday picked up a Turkish pilot who bailed out of his F-16 fighter after being intercepted by Greek warplanes over the Aegean Sea, Greek radios said.
The defence ministry said earlier a Turkish fighter pilot had radioed he was abandoning his plane after been intercepted by two Greek Mirage 2000s near the Greek island of Chios.
Defence ministry officials said the pilot was alive and was being taken to a hospital on the island of Chios, just off the Turkish coast.

The incident occurred on the last day of joint Greek-Cypriot military exercises -- "Nikiforos" on Cyprus and "Toxotis" in the southern Aegean. The exercises stem from a 1993 military pact between Greece and the militarily divided island of Cyprus.

Greece reported more than 50 airspace violations since Monday, when the exercises started. Greek fighter planes were scrambled more than 40 times to intercept Turkish planes on Monday, the defence ministry said.
